body.translated_text: <s>Āmaraughaśāsana</s>
The descent of the upward <s>śakti</s> (power) is known through the four <s>kandas</s> (bulbs). // 1

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* yac candraprabhavaṃ varāmbaragataṃ yal liṅgasaṃjñaṃ jalaṃ sa prāṇas tadadhaḥ sthiraṃ ca kamalaṃ dhatte mukhordhvaṃ hṛdi || 1.1
children.translated_text: That water which arises from the moon, situated in the excellent sky, which is known as <s>liṅga</s> — that <s>prāṇa</s>, below it a steady lotus holds [it] upward from the mouth in the heart. || 1.1

children.text: * baddhvā kumbhakam ātmagāḍharacitaṃ tad brahmanāḍīgataṃ hy ānetuṃ vadane ṣaḍadhvagakalā saivaṃvidhā sāraṇā || 1.2]
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), deeply fashioned within the self, that which has entered the <s>brahmanāḍī</s> — indeed, to bring it to the mouth, the sixfold-path digit (<s>ṣaḍadhvagakalā</s>) — this is that kind of <s>sāraṇā</s> (channeling). || 1.2

body.translated_text: The sixfold-path [technique] is described. // 2

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* ghaṇṭākoṭikapolakoṭarakuṭījihvāgramadhyāśrayāc chaṅkhinyāgatarājadantavivaraṃ prāntordhvavaktreṇa yat || 2.1
children.translated_text: From the abode at the tip of the tongue, the tip of the bell, the hollow of the cheek, the cavity of the palate — through the <s>śaṅkhinī</s> [nāḍī], reaching the opening of the front teeth, that which is at the edge of the upper mouth — || 2.1

children.text: * saṃprāptaṃ hanurandhramūlavidhinā yac candratoyaṃ mukhe tat sarvaṃ ravikālarūpasadane rakṣet parā sāraṇā || 2.2]
children.translated_text: Having reached the moon-water in the mouth by the method of the root of the jaw-opening, one should preserve all that in the abode of the sun-time form — this is the supreme <s>sāraṇā</s>. || 2.2

body.translated_text: By another practice, the supreme <s>sāraṇā</s> is described. // 3

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* nṛtyan nityordhvajihvo yadi pibati pumān vaktradhārāmṛtaughaṃ susvādaṃ śītalāṅgaṃ duritabhayaharaṃ kṣutpipāsāvināśi || 3.1
children.translated_text: If a man, always dancing with tongue raised upward, drinks the stream of nectar flowing from the mouth — sweet-tasting, cooling the body, removing the fear of sin, destroying hunger and thirst — || 3.1

children.text: * piṇḍasthairyaṃ yad asmād bhavati bata mahāmṛtyurogā dravante daurbhāgyaṃ yāti nāśaṃ harati viṣajarāṃ yāti kāle bhramitvā || 3.2]
children.translated_text: From this comes steadiness of the body; indeed, the great diseases of death dissolve; misfortune goes to destruction; it removes the poison of old age; [the practitioner] goes [beyond], having wandered in time. || 3.2

body.translated_text: After <s>sāraṇā</s>, [the next] <s>sāraṇā</s> is described. // 4

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* jihvāgraṃ tv atha rājadantavivaraṃ nītvā tato ghaṇṭikāṃ saṃsthāpya pratijihvaparva śaśino mārge kalāṃ ca kṣipet || 4.1
children.translated_text: Then, having taken the tip of the tongue to the opening of the front teeth, then placing it at the bell (<s>ghaṇṭikā</s>), at the joint of the epiglottis, one should cast the digit (<s>kalā</s>) in the path of the moon — || 4.1

children.text: * evaṃsāraṇike patanti ca sudhādhārāḥ punaḥ ṣaṇmukhagāndhārāpy atha tatkalāpamathanaṃ nāḍīmukhojjṛmbhaṇam || 4.2]
children.translated_text: In this kind of channeling, the streams of nectar fall; again, the six-faced <s>gāndhāra</s> [practice], and then the churning of that bundle of digits, the opening of the mouths of the <s>nāḍīs</s>. || 4.2

body.translated_text: After <s>sāraṇā</s>, <s>pratisāraṇā</s> (counter-channeling) is described. // 5

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* prāṇavātena nītvordhvaṃ koṭare candrajāṃ kalām || 5.1
children.translated_text: Having led upward by the <s>prāṇa</s> wind, the moon-born digit in the cavity — || 5.1

children.text: * manthitāṃ divyajātāṃ ca tena gāndhārakarmaṇā || 5.2]
children.translated_text: Churned and divinely born — by that <s>gāndhāra</s> practice. || 5.2

body.translated_text: After <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>pratisāraṇā</s> is described. // 6

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* nāsāpaścimamārgavāhapavanāt prāṇe 'tidīrghīkṛte candrāmbu pratisāraṇāṃ sukṛtinaḥ prāgghaṇṭikāyāḥ pathaḥ || 6.1
children.translated_text: By the wind moving through the posterior nasal passage, when the <s>prāṇa</s> is greatly extended, the virtuous ones [perform] <s>pratisāraṇā</s> of the moon-water, from the path before the bell (<s>ghaṇṭikā</s>) — || 6.1

children.text: * siñcan kālaviśālavahnivaśagaṃ bhūtvā sa nāḍīśataṃ tat kāryaṃ kurute punar navatanuṃ jīrṇadrumaskandhavat || 6.2]
children.translated_text: Sprinkling [it], having come under the power of the vast fire of time, through a hundred <s>nāḍīs</s>, it performs that action, [producing] a new body again, like the trunk of a withered tree. || 6.2

body.translated_text: After <s>pratisāraṇā</s>, <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s> (conch-channeling) is described. // 7

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* protkṣiptaṃ vṛṣaṇasya golakayugaṃ madhye dhvajaṃ proddhvajaṃ nityordhve bata śaṅkhasāraṇavidhau vaktraṃ vidheyaṃ nijam || 7.1
children.translated_text: The pair of globes of the testicles raised upward, the shaft erect in the middle — in the method of <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>, one should always keep the mouth directed upward. || 7.1

children.text: * sarvasthānaśarīrabandhanavaśāt skandhoddhṛtānāṃ yathā nāḍīnāṃ mukhataḥ sudhānidhijalaṃ siñcann adho gacchati || 7.2]
children.translated_text: By the binding of the body at all points, from the mouths of the <s>nāḍīs</s> lifted from the shoulders, the water of the nectar-reservoir, sprinkling downward, descends. || 7.2

body.translated_text: By another practice, <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s> is described. // 8

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* vṛṣaṇākarṣaṇaṃ kāryam athavā śaṅkhasāraṇā || 8.1
children.translated_text: The drawing up of the testicles should be performed, or alternatively <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s> — || 8.1

children.text: * bodhanaṃ caiva kuṇḍalyās tiṣṭhec caivotkaṭāsanam || 8.2]
children.translated_text: And the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> (the coiled one); and one should remain in <s>utkaṭāsana</s> (the fierce posture). || 8.2

body.translated_text: After <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>, <s>mahāsāraṇā</s> (the great channeling) is described. // 9

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* paścād āsanaśuddhavātanikarān ādāya kaṇṭhavraṇāt saṃsthāpyā ravimaṇḍale tu bhujagī saṃbhūtanāḍītrayāt || 9.1
children.translated_text: Having taken from behind the collection of pure winds from the seat, from the wound of the throat, the serpent-goddess (<s>bhujagī</s>) should be established in the solar disc, having arisen from the three <s>nāḍīs</s> — || 9.1

children.text: * devī madhyapathoditā prakurute kampaṃ tato mūrchanāṃ dūrakarṣaṇadarśanaṃ śrutigaṇāṃś cānyā mahāsāraṇā || 9.2]
children.translated_text: The goddess, having arisen in the middle path, produces trembling, then fainting, distant attraction and vision, and the groups of scriptures — this is the other great <s>sāraṇā</s>. || 9.2

body.translated_text: By another practice, <s>mahāsāraṇā</s> is described. // 10

children.text: Komm. zum āmaraughaśāsana
* ādhārāmbujakośakandabhujagī saṃbhūya nāḍītrayāt candrārkodbhavanāḍikordhvayugalaṃ cādvaitapathyāgatam || 10.1
children.translated_text: The serpent-goddess (<s>bhujagī</s>), arising from the three <s>nāḍīs</s> from the bulb-sheath of the base lotus, and the upper pair of channels born of the moon and sun, having come through the path of non-duality — || 10.1

children.text: * tatraivāṅgulibhir nipīḍya kramaśaḥ śāntiṃ mano mārutaṃ candro yāti raviṃ tataś ca bhuvane tulyā mahāsāraṇā || 10.2
children.translated_text: There, pressing gradually with the fingers, [achieving] peace of mind and breath — the moon goes to the sun; and then in the world, the equal great <s>sāraṇā</s>. || 10.2

children.text: * sūryāntaḥ śaśivīcidantavadanaprāntaplavaughoragī saṃprāpte pavanātisaṅgaharaṇe kṣipraṃ tato dhāvitā || 10.3
children.translated_text: The serpent, a flood of waves flowing at the edge of the mouth through the teeth and moon-rays within the sun — when the excessive gathering of wind is attained, then swiftly driven — || 10.3

children.text: * śrīmanmadhyapathāntato vidadhatī kampādi kopānvitā tasyaivāśrayayāyino 'pi śaśino dattā sudhā saṃmatā || 10.4
children.translated_text: The glorious one, manifesting from within the middle path, producing trembling and the like, filled with fury, bestows the well-regarded nectar of the moon which follows its own abode. || 10.4

children.text: * ādau śoṣaṇiko 'tra sāraṇam ataḥ kāryaṃ mahāsāraṇaṃ kartavyaṃ pratisāraṇaṃ ca guruṇā nirdiṣṭamārgaṃ kramāt || 10.5
children.translated_text: First, the desiccation [practice]; then <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed; <s>mahāsāraṇā</s> should be done; and <s>pratisāraṇā</s>, in the path indicated by the <s>guru</s>, in sequence — || 10.5

children.text: * paścād eva ca śaṅkhasāraṇavidhau kāryaṃ mahāsāraṇaṃ sammūrchā vitatākṛtiḥ pratidinaṃ velātrayaṃ dīyatām || 10.6
children.translated_text: And afterwards, in the method of <s>śaṅkhasāraṇā</s>, <s>mahāsāraṇā</s> should be performed; fainting [occurs], the form is extended; three times daily it should be given. || 10.6

children.text: * ākuñcyāgajakāmarūpam acalaṃ bandhatvajātaṃ tanau nātyūrdhve caturaṅgulāgravidite sthāne hṛdā prāṇite || 10.7
children.translated_text: Contracting the elephant-form of desire, immovable, born of binding in the body, at a place known to be four fingers above, not too high, enlivened by the heart — || 10.7

children.text: * dantair bandhurite ca vātayugale praśleṣaṇāśleṣaṇāt nābhigranthivimokṣapātasahaje mārge manaḥsiddhayaḥ || 10.8
children.translated_text: With the teeth clenched, and when the two winds are in contact and not in contact, on the natural path of the release of the navel-knot's fall — [arise] the <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) of the mind. || 10.8

children.text: * dūrākāravisarpite ca pavane nābheś ca mārgasthite bandheṣu triṣu satsu so 'pi śithile madhyaprabodhe sati || 10.9
children.translated_text: And when the wind has crept far away and is stationed on the path from the navel, when the three <s>bandhas</s> (locks) are present and that [wind] is relaxed, when the awakening of the middle [channel] occurs — || 10.9

children.text: * kṣipraṃ ca dhriyate dvipīṭhamaruto 'py ūrdhvakramākarṣaṇe saṃyukto gaticittaśoṣaṇam ataḥ prāpye 'nile tiṣṭhati || 10.10
children.translated_text: Swiftly the two-seated wind is held, even in the upward drawing process; joined with the desiccation of movement and mind — then, when the wind is attained, [the yogin] remains. || 10.10

children.text: * mūle mūlordhvacakre vṛṣaṇakulatale vahnimātaṅgakūle kampakṣobhabhramāḍhye dhvanitaparicayaṃ gharmapātordhvaroma || 10.11
children.translated_text: At the root, in the root-upper <s>cakra</s>, at the base of the testicle-group, at the slope of the fire-elephant — rich with trembling, agitation, and whirling; familiarity with sound, heat-fall, hair standing upward — || 10.11

children.text: * bhūmityāgaṃ kavitvaṃ parapuraviśanaṃ vaśyam ākarṣaṇaṃ ca hy evaṃ vā cetanāptā prabhavati nikhilā khecaratvapratiṣṭhā || 10.12
children.translated_text: Abandonment of the earth, poetic power, entering another's city, control, attraction — and thus, when consciousness is attained, all establishment in the state of <s>khecara</s> (moving in space) arises. || 10.12

children.text: * dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca tat || 10.13
children.translated_text: Two aspects of <s>Brahman</s> are to be known: <s>śabdabrahman</s> (sound-Brahman) and the supreme (<s>para</s>). || 10.13

children.text: * hṛdaye parame dhāmni madhye tu ravicandramāḥ || 10.14
children.translated_text: In the heart, in the supreme abode, in the middle are the sun and moon. || 10.14

children.text: * nādaṃ tu taṃ gṛhītvā ca caitanyaṃ tatra yojayet || 10.15
children.translated_text: Having grasped that <s>nāda</s> (inner sound), one should unite consciousness with it. || 10.15

children.text: * dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca tat || 10.16
children.translated_text: Two aspects of <s>Brahman</s> are to be known: <s>śabdabrahman</s> and the supreme. || 10.16

children.text: * śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati || 10.17
children.translated_text: One who is skilled in <s>śabdabrahman</s> attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. || 10.17

children.text: * anyat sarvaṃ parityajya śabdabrahma sadābhyaset || 10.18
children.translated_text: Abandoning everything else, one should always practice <s>śabdabrahman</s>. || 10.18

children.text: * svasaṃvedyam asaṃvedyaṃ śabdabrahma dvidhā sthitam || 10.19
children.translated_text: <s>Śabdabrahman</s> exists in two forms: self-perceivable and imperceivable. || 10.19

children.text: * cinoti prathamaḥ śabdaś ciñcinoti dvitīyakaḥ || 10.20
children.translated_text: The first sound is 'ci'; the second is 'ciñci' — || 10.20

children.text: * vivaraś ca tṛtīyaḥ syāc chaṅkhaśabdaś caturthakaḥ || 10.21
children.translated_text: The third should be 'vivara' (opening); and the fourth is the conch-sound — || 10.21

children.text: * pañcamo meghanirghoṣaḥ ṣaṣṭham etad udīraṇam || 10.22
children.translated_text: The fifth is the rumbling of clouds; and the sixth is this utterance — || 10.22

children.text: * saptamaṃ kāṃsyatālākhyaṃ meghaśabdas tathāṣṭamam || 10.23
children.translated_text: The seventh is called the sound of brass cymbal; the eighth likewise is the cloud-sound — || 10.23

children.text: * navamo 'py agnidāhaś ca daśamo dundubhisvanaḥ || 10.24
children.translated_text: The ninth is also the burning of fire; and the tenth is the sound of the drum (<s>dundubhi</s>). || 10.24

children.text: * anāhataninādo 'yaṃ pavanāntavinirgataḥ || 10.25
children.translated_text: This is the <s>anāhata</s> (unstruck) sound, arising from within the end of the breath. || 10.25

children.text: * dhvanitena vinā yas tu nādaś caivam apaṇḍitaḥ || 10.26
children.translated_text: But without resonance, that <s>nāda</s> is thus [perceived by] the unlearned — || 10.26

children.text: * cinoti rasam uddhṛtya ciñcinoti bhagāśritam || 10.27
children.translated_text: 'Ci' extracts the essence; 'ciñci' is situated in the generative organ — || 10.27

children.text: * virasāṃśena saṃprāptaṃ meghaśabdena cāviśet || 10.28
children.translated_text: Having arrived with the portion of heroic essence (<s>vīra-rasa</s>), one should enter with the cloud-sound — || 10.28

children.text: * majjāṃ patati nirghoṣaḥ saṃsthitodadhibhīṣaṇaḥ || 10.29
children.translated_text: The thundering falls into the marrow, terrifying like a standing ocean — || 10.29

children.text: * kāṃsyatāle nabhaḥśabdaḥ prāṇameghadhvaniḥ kramāt || 10.30
children.translated_text: In the brass cymbal [stage], the sky-sound; the sound of the <s>prāṇa</s>-cloud, in sequence — || 10.30

children.text: * jīvaś caivāgnidāhaḥ syān mokṣaḥ samaraso bhavet || 10.31
children.translated_text: The individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) becomes the fire-burning; liberation becomes equal-savored (<s>samarasa</s>). || 10.31

children.text: * viśuddham ittham ātmānaṃ paśyeta cātmanātmani || 10.32
children.translated_text: Thus, one should see the purified self, by the self, in the self. || 10.32

children.text: * prathame janavātsalyaṃ dvitīye roganāśanam || 10.33
children.translated_text: In the first [stage], affection for people; in the second, destruction of diseases — || 10.33

children.text: * tṛtīyena kavitvaṃ ca dūrākarṣaṃ caturthake || 10.34
children.translated_text: By the third, poetic power; and in the fourth, distant attraction — || 10.34

children.text: * pañcame vāci kāmitvaṃ ṣaṣṭhe bhūmiṃ parityajet || 10.35
children.translated_text: In the fifth, wish-fulfillment in speech; in the sixth, one abandons the earth — || 10.35

children.text: * saptame dūram ālokya cāṣṭame vajravad bhavet || 10.36
children.translated_text: In the seventh, seeing far; and in the eighth, one becomes like a thunderbolt — || 10.36

children.text: * navame sphurate kāyo daśame sāmarasyakam || 10.37
children.translated_text: In the ninth, the body shines forth; in the tenth, the state of equal essence (<s>sāmarasya</s>). || 10.37

children.text: * pṛthvīmadhye bhavet pṛthvī cāpām āpas tathaiva ca || 10.38
children.translated_text: In the midst of earth, there is earth; and of water, water likewise — || 10.38

children.text: * tejomadhye bhavet tejo vāyur vāyau pralīyate || 10.39
children.translated_text: In the midst of fire, there is fire; wind dissolves into wind — || 10.39

children.text: * ākāśo līyate sarvaḥ satattvaḥ piṇḍasaṃgrahaḥ || 10.40
children.translated_text: All space dissolves; the true essence is the collection of the body. || 10.40

children.text: * anāhato divārātrau dhvanate tu dhanaṃjayaḥ || 10.41
children.translated_text: The <s>anāhata</s> [sound] resonates day and night, [carried by] <s>Dhanañjaya</s> [wind] — || 10.41

children.text: * tatrārūḍho yadā yogī prāpnuyāt paramaṃ padam || 10.42]
children.translated_text: When the <s>yogī</s> who has ascended there attains the supreme state. || 10.42

body.text: ayaṃ prakṛtibhedaḥ pṛthvī āpaḥ tejaḥ vāyuḥ ākāśaś ca iti śarīre pañcaguṇāḥ mahābhūtāni bhavanti tatraiva tāni pañcavidhāni bhavanti // 11
body.translated_text: This is the division of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature): earth, water, fire, wind, and space — thus in the body there are five-qualitied <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements); therein they exist in five kinds. // 11

body.text: asthi māṃsaṃ tvak nāḍī romāṇi iti pañcaguṇā pṛthivī // 12
body.translated_text: Bone, flesh, skin, <s>nāḍīs</s>, and hair — these are the five qualities of earth. // 12
Saliva, urine, tears, sweat, and perspiration — these are the five qualities of water. // 13

body.text: kṣudhā tṛṣṇā nidrā ālasyaṃ kāntiś ca iti pañcaguṇaṃ tejaḥ // 14
body.translated_text: Hunger, thirst, sleep, laziness, and radiance — these are the five qualities of fire. // 14

body.text: dhāvanaṃ valganam ākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ nirodhaś ceti pañcaguṇo vāyuḥ // 15
body.translated_text: Running, leaping, contracting, extending, and restraining — these are the five qualities of wind. // 15

body.text: rāgo dveṣo lajjā bhayaṃ mohaś ceti pañcaguṇa ākāśaḥ iti pañcaguṇālaṅkṛtāni pañcatattvāni // 16
body.translated_text: Passion, hatred, shame, fear, and delusion — these are the five qualities of space. Thus, the five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) are adorned with five qualities. // 16

body.text: śabdaḥ sparśaḥ rasaḥ rūpaṃ gandhaś ceti pañca bhūtaguṇāḥ // 17
body.translated_text: Sound, touch, taste, form, and smell — these are the five elemental qualities. // 17

The nine dramatic sentiments (<s>rasas</s>) beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) — the emotional states (<s>bhāvas</s>) beginning with <s>hāsya</s> (humor) belong to those beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. // 18
Pungent, bitter, astringent, sour, sweet, and salty—these are the six tastes. // 19
Auspicious and inauspicious—these are the two types of <s>karma</s> (action). // 20
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>—these are the ten vital airs. // 21

<s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Suṣumnā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Hastijihvā</s>, <s>Yaśasvinī</s>, <s>Pūṣā</s>, <s>Alambusā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, and others—there are seventy-two thousand <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels). // 22
Creation, maintenance, and dissolution—these are the three paths. // 23

body.text: asthisaṃcayaṃ ṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ śatatrayam asty asya prāṇena saṃbandhaḥ // 24
body.translated_text: The collection of bones numbers three hundred and sixty; their connection is with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). // 24
Desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, arrogance, and ego—these are the seven bondages. // 25

Discrimination, awareness, contentment, joy, rapture, patience, tranquility, meditation, knowledge, elation, passion, dispassion, bliss, trembling, fainting, transformation, mental impressions, and so forth—these are the forms of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // 26
The body hairs number three and a half crores (thirty-five million). // 27
<s>Vāta</s> (wind), <s>Pitta</s> (bile), and <s>Śleṣman</s> (phlegm)—these are the three constitutions. // 28

body.text: vātaḥ prāṇaprakṛtiḥ pittaṃ hutāśanodbhūtaṃ śleṣmā nirodhāt bhavati // 29
body.translated_text: <s>Vāta</s> is the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>pitta</s> arises from fire; <s>śleṣman</s> arises from obstruction. // 29

body.text: tvak asṛk māṃsaṃ medaḥ asthi majjā śukraṃ prāṇo jīvaḥ śaktiḥ iti daśa dhātavaḥ // 30
body.translated_text: Skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), and <s>śakti</s> (power)—these are the ten <s>dhātus</s> (constituents). // 30

body.text: prāṇarandhradvayaṃ locanarandhradvayaṃ karṇarandhradvayaṃ mukharandhradvayam utsargarandhradvayam iti daśa dvārāṇi // 31
body.translated_text: Two nostril openings, two eye openings, two ear openings, two mouth openings, and two excretory openings—these are the ten gates. // 31

body.text: atha daśamadvāraṃ dvividhaṃ śukramārgam amṛtaṃ kālamārgaś ceti brahmadaṇḍamūle raviśaśimadhye bhagākāram asti tasmād āgatabrahmadaṇḍāśritaṃ paścimaliṅgam asti paścimaśabdena sthānam asti tasya madhye liṅgākāram asti // 32
body.translated_text: Now, the tenth gate is of two kinds: the path of semen and the path of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), which is the path of death. At the base of the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s> (spinal column), between the sun and moon, there exists a <s>bhaga</s>-shaped form. From that, situated along the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s>, is the posterior <s>liṅga</s>. By the word "posterior" is meant the place; in its center exists a <s>liṅga</s>-shaped form. // 32

body.text: puruṣāṇāṃ retomārgaḥ strīṇāṃ rajomārgaḥ sahaiva tena brahmadaṇḍarekhāśritapuṣpasamaye sarvavyāpakanāḍīsamūhāgataṃ kāminīrajaḥ sravati // 33
body.translated_text: For men, it is the path of semen; for women, the path of menstrual fluid. Along with that, at the time of flowering situated along the line of the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s>, the menstrual fluid of the desiring woman flows, having come through the assemblage of all-pervading <s>nāḍīs</s>. // 33

body.text: tatraiva kāmaviṣaharanirañjanānāṃ saṃyogaṃ bījapātāt ānandāgamaḥ pralayakālaviṣakālayoḥ kartā nirañjanaś ca iti // 34
body.translated_text: There indeed, through the union of desire, poison, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless One), from the fall of the seed comes the arrival of bliss. The agent of both the time of dissolution and the time of poison is <s>Nirañjana</s>. // 34
When the mind is penetrated by the three <s>śaktis</s> (powers), through the seed of <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless One), // 35
whoever performs the bliss of the state of <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) worship, he is <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love). // 36
When the mind is satisfied, there is liberation of the mind; when the fire resides in the upward path, // 37
the semen moved by <s>Udāna</s> (upward breath) is known as the poison of the line of death. // 38
That which exists in the center of the mind, resting in the space of a hundredth part of a hair-tip, // 39
free from manifold states of being—that is declared to be <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless One). // 40
The <s>śakti</s> (power) rests in <s>Nirañjana</s>; by that subtle <s>śakti</s>, supported by her, // 41

body.text: manasy āśrayatāmeti jñeyaṃ śaktitrayaṃ tu tat // 42
body.translated_text: it comes to rest in the mind—this should be known as the threefold <s>śakti</s> (power). // 42

body.text: śaktitrayodbhavaṃ bījaṃ bījāt kāmo viṣaṃ tataḥ // 43
body.translated_text: The seed arises from the three <s>śaktis</s>; from the seed comes desire, and from that, poison. // 43

body.text: kāmaḥ sṛṣṭitayā prokto viṣaṃ mṛtyupadaṃ bhavet // 44
body.translated_text: Desire is declared to be in the nature of creation; poison becomes the state of death. // 44

body.text: kiṃ bahunā kāmaviṣaharanirañjanānāṃ brahmadaṇḍamūlāṅkure nivāsaḥ ebhir yad amukho mokṣaḥ bhasmībhūtasya dehasya punar āgamanakāryaṃ nāsti // 45
body.translated_text: Why say more? The abode of desire, poison, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Nirañjana</s> is in the sprout at the base of the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s> (spinal column). Through these, there is direct liberation; for the body that has become ashes, there is no need to return again. // 45

body.text: aho mūrkhatā lokasya kecid vadanti śubhāśubhakarmavicchedanaṃ mokṣaḥ // 46
body.translated_text: Alas, the foolishness of the world! Some say that liberation is the cessation of auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s> (action). // 46
Some say that liberation depends on the recitation of the <s>Vedas</s>. // 47
Some say that liberation is characterized by supportlessness. // 48

Some say that liberation, arising through practices connected with the techniques of meditative arts, is characterized by form, <s>bindu</s> (point), <s>nāda</s> (sound), consciousness, body, and space. // 49
Some say that liberation is characterized by the bliss arising from worship, the worshipper, wine, meat, and other sexual practices. // 50
Some say: // 51
liberation is characterized by the movement of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> aroused from the <s>mūlakanda</s> (root bulb). // 52

body.text: kecid vadanti susamadṛṣṭinipātalakṣaṇo mokṣaḥ ity evaṃvidhabhāvanāśritalakṣaṇo mokṣo na bhavati // 53
body.translated_text: Some say that liberation is characterized by the descent of the perfectly balanced gaze. Liberation characterized by such types of contemplation does not truly exist. // 53

body.text: atha mokṣapadaṃ kathyate yatra sahajasamādhikrameṇa manasā manaḥ samālokyate sa eva mokṣaḥ // 54
body.translated_text: Now the state of liberation is described: where the mind perceives the mind through the process of <s>sahaja-samādhi</s> (innate absorption)—that alone is liberation. // 54

body.text: kāmaviṣaharasthānaṃ mānasodbhavaḥ manomadhye kāraṇaṃ kāraṇāt utpattisthitipralayāḥ pravartante // 55
body.translated_text: The abode of desire, poison, and <s>Hara</s> is of mental origin; the cause lies within the mind, and from that cause proceed creation, maintenance, and dissolution. // 55
And the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord) has said: // 56
"O <s>Devī</s>, in the state of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), the mind is the seed of <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless One). // 57
The <s>yogī</s> established in the path of death, having known this, should practice the action." // 58

body.text: iti jīvanmuktipadam anena mārgeṇa sthiratvaṃ bhavati // 59
body.translated_text: Thus, the state of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) becomes stable through this path. // 59

body.text: athādhāraṇakarmoditaśaṅkhinībhedavyavasthāvyākhyā gudameḍhrāntare trikoṇatridhāvartabhagamaṇḍalam ucyate tatra ādhāragranthaya ekadvitrayaś ceti ekadvitrayāṇāṃ madhye granthīnām upāntare catuṣpatraṃ padmam adhomukhaṃ tiṣṭhati tatra karṇikāmadhye mṛṇālasūtraparimāṇā śaṅkhāvartā tatra pravālāṅkurasannibhā dvitrināḍībhūtā kuṇḍalinī śaktiḥ caitanyabījamukhaṃ gatvā suptā // 60
body.translated_text: Now the explanation of the arrangement of the piercing of <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> arising from the act of <s>ādhāraṇa</s> (holding): Between the anus and the genitals is described the triangular, triple-whirled <s>bhaga-maṇḍala</s> (vulva-circle). There, the knots of the <s>ādhāra</s> (support) are one, two, and three. In the middle of these one, two, and three knots, near the knots, a four-petaled lotus stands facing downward. There, in the middle of the pericarp, with the dimensions of a lotus-stalk fiber, spiraling like a conch shell, resembling a coral sprout, having become two or three <s>nāḍīs</s>, the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> <s>śakti</s>, having gone to the opening of the seed of consciousness, lies sleeping. // 60
There, in the middle of the three paths, she is established in subtle form. // 61
Having the appearance of a spider's thread, she extends to the navel region. // 62
Measuring four finger-breadths, she is coiled eightfold. // 63
Throbbing in the center of the navel, she branches forth into many sub-branches. // 64

children.text: daśanāḍyāśritaṃ cakraṃ nābhimadhye prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: The <s>cakra</s> (wheel) supported by ten <s>nāḍīs</s> is declared to be in the center of the navel.

children.text: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva suṣumnā ca tṛtīyakā // 65
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, and <s>Suṣumnā</s> as the third— // 65

body.translated_text: these are established in the upward path, hanging from the great branch. // 66
<s>Alambusā</s> prevails as one, hanging from the great branch. // 67

body.text: praṇītā sā hy anekais tu brahmāvartena saṃsthitā // 68
body.translated_text: She is led forth by many and is established in the <s>Brahmāvarta</s> (spiral of <s>Brahman</s>). // 68

body.text: brahmadaṇḍacakreṇāsau kapālakarparaṃ yāvat tasmin kapālakarpare candramaṇḍalāntargataṃ kapālaliṅgaṃ lampikāsthānordhve 'mṛtadhārām abhisravati mastakamadhye garbhe tiṣṭhati tad evāmṛtaṃ rājadantamaye śaṅkhinī brahmadaṇḍatale damayitvā sravati // 69
body.translated_text: By the wheel of the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s> (spinal column), it reaches up to the skull-bowl. In that skull-bowl, within the lunar disc, is the skull-<s>liṅga</s>; above the place of the uvula, it causes the stream of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) to flow. It resides in the womb at the center of the head. That very nectar, having been restrained by <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> at the palatal bone, flows at the base of the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s>. // 69

body.text: ekaṃ mukharandhraṃ rājadantāntare etad eva śaṅkhinīmukhaṃ daśamadvāram ity ucyate // 70
body.translated_text: One mouth opening between the palatal bones—this is the mouth of <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, which is called the tenth gate. // 70

body.text: yatra ca mūlabhagamaṇḍalānte kuṇḍalinī śaktir vinirgatā tatra vāmabhāgodbhavasomanāḍikā dakṣiṇabhāgodbhavasūryanāḍikā candro vāmāṅgavyāpakaḥ sūryo dakṣiṇāṅgavyāpakaḥ candro vāmāṅge vāmanāsāpuṭaṃ sūryo dakṣiṇāṅge dakṣiṇanāsāpuṭam ity evaṃ sūryacandrau vyavasthitau // 71
body.translated_text: Where the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> <s>śakti</s> emerges at the end of the root <s>bhaga-maṇḍala</s>, there the lunar <s>nāḍī</s> arises from the left side and the solar <s>nāḍī</s> from the right side. The moon pervades the left body, the sun pervades the right body. The moon on the left side corresponds to the left nostril, the sun on the right side to the right nostril—thus the sun and moon are established. // 71

body.text: yatra mūlakande pavanodayaḥ manasa udayaḥ tapanodayaḥ jīvodayaḥ śabdodayaḥ mātṛkākṣarodayaś ceti // 72
body.translated_text: In the <s>mūlakanda</s> (root bulb) arise the wind, the mind, heat, the individual soul, sound, and the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters (alphabet). // 72
In the center of the mind, the object of sleep, whose function is desire, is <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless One), the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self). // 73
The wind arises from the <s>mūlakanda</s> (root bulb), born of the paths of the moon and sun. // 74
Established in the support of <s>śakti</s>, it goes forth, piercing the <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s> (spinal column). // 75
That <s>śakti</s> which is in the <s>mūlakanda</s> (root bulb), having a coiled form, // 76
this rising, whirling wind is called <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) by the wise. // 77
She who is the serpent power, stirred by the staff of the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) and by upright forces, // 78

body.text: mūrchitā sā śivaṃ vetti prāṇair evaṃ vyavasthitā // 79
body.translated_text: when she swoons, she knows <s>Śiva</s>, thus established by the vital breaths. // 79

body.text: janmāvasthānād adho liṅgaḥ sa cādhārakandajātimadhyasthito guhya ūrdhve bhavati tasyordhve liṅgasthānaṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ nābhimaṇḍale maṇipūrakasyordhvabhāge 'nalakaḥ tenoddaṇḍakādyaṃ samāgacchati adhaḥpradeśe maṇipūrakasya dakṣiṇapaścimavarti amedhyasthānam madhye nābheḥ kandaḥ tatra padmākṛtiḥ tatra śarīranāḍīnām ādhāraḥ kathyate hṛdaye pṛthivītattvaṃ pītavarṇaṃ madhye kadambagolakākṛti tatra cittaviśrāntisthānaṃ tad eva analacakram kaṇṭhe codakapravāhapūrṇam ātmatattvaṃ tad viśuddhisthānam tālumadhye dīpaśikhākāraḥ sadoddyotaḥ tat tejastattvam kapālakandarāṅkure vāyutattvam nāsāgre ākāśatattvam tasyordhve

children.text: ājñāsthānam ājñāsthānāntare granthiṣoḍaśāntare amṛtā ṣoḍaśī kalā tadantare vālāgraśatadhāśrayā ante tasyordhve kalānte binduḥ bindubhedād anantaraṃ śṛṃgāṭakākṛtir mastakasyoddeśas tasmin cittalayasthānam cittasya śarīrabandhanādvayopetas trailokyavihāraḥ tasyāśritā jñānaśaktiḥ evaṃ śaktitrayālaṃkṛtaś ciddarpaṇapratibimbaḥ samo vividhabhāvakalākalitaḥ saṃsāraceṣṭāvalokanakuśalaḥ suptāvasthāyāṃ rūpī jalacandravat dṛśyate yaḥ sa paramātmā sarvavyāpī maheśvaraḥ caturdaśavidhabhūtagrāmakartā ca iti so 'yaṃ paramātmā // 80
children.translated_text: is the <s>Ājñā</s> place. Within the <s>Ājñā</s> place, within the sixteen knots, is the sixteenth <s>kalā</s> (digit) of nectar. Within that, resting in the hundredth part of a hair-tip, at the end, above that, at the end of the <s>kalā</s>, is the <s>bindu</s> (point). Immediately after the piercing of the <s>bindu</s> is the crossroads-shaped region of the head—therein is the place of dissolution of the mind. The mind, endowed with the pair of bodily bonds, roams the three worlds. Dependent on it is <s>jñānaśakti</s> (the power of knowledge). Thus, adorned by the threefold <s>śakti</s>, a reflection in the mirror of consciousness, balanced, pervaded by the arts of manifold states of being, skilled in observing the activities of worldly existence, in the state of sleep appearing with form like the moon in water—that is the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), all-pervading <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), the creator of the fourteen types of beings. This is that <s>Paramātmā</s>. // 80

body.translated_text: Below the place of birth is the <s>liṅga</s>, which is secret, situated in the middle of the root support (<s>ādhāra-kanda</s>); above, it becomes manifest. Above that is the <s>liṅga</s>-place, <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>; in the navel region is the upper part of <s>Maṇipūraka</s>, where the fire element resides—from there the upright force arises. In the lower region of <s>Maṇipūraka</s>, to the right and behind, is the place of impurity. In the center of the navel is the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), which has a lotus shape; there the support of the body's <s>nāḍīs</s> is said to be. In the heart is the earth element, yellow in color, having the shape of a <s>kadamba</s> flower ball—there is the resting place of the mind; that itself is the fire <s>cakra</s>. In the throat, filled with the flow of water, is the self-element; that is the <s>Viśuddhi</s> place. In the middle of the palate, having the form of a lamp flame, ever-shining, is the fire element. In the sprout of the skull-cave is the wind element. At the tip of the nose is the space element. Above that
